# name: test/sql/transaction/postgres_failed_rollback_releases_transaction.test
# description: a ROLLBACK that loses its Postgres connection still releases its DuckLake transaction and the metadata connection it holds
# group: [transaction]

require ducklake

require parquet

require postgres_scanner

require-env DUCKLAKE_CI

require-env DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION

test-env DATA_PATH {TEST_DIR}

statement ok
ATTACH '{DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION}' AS pg

statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS failed_rollback CASCADE')

statement ok
ATTACH 'ducklake:{DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION} application_name=failed_rollback' AS dl
(DATA_PATH '{DATA_PATH}/failed_rollback', METADATA_SCHEMA 'failed_rollback', DATA_INLINING_ROW_LIMIT 10)

statement ok
CREATE TABLE dl.t (i INTEGER)

statement ok
SET VARIABLE connections = (SELECT count FROM duckdb_connection_count())

statement ok
BEGIN

statement ok
INSERT INTO dl.t VALUES (1)

# the metadata connections of the lake are gone before the rollback
query I
SELECT count(*) > 0 AND bool_and(terminated) FROM postgres_query('pg',
'SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid, 5000) AS terminated FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE datname = current_database() AND application_name = ''failed_rollback''')
----
true

statement maybe
ROLLBACK
----
connection

query I
SELECT count = getvariable('connections') FROM duckdb_connection_count()
----
true

statement ok
INSERT INTO dl.t VALUES (2)

query I
SELECT * FROM dl.t
----
2

statement ok
DETACH dl

statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'DROP SCHEMA failed_rollback CASCADE')

# name: test/sql/transaction/partition_commit_retry_remap.test
# description: data files keep a valid partition id when a commit attempt is retried after a concurrent snapshot
# group: [transaction]

require ducklake

require parquet

test-env DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION {TEST_DIR}/{UUID}.db

test-env DATA_PATH {TEST_DIR}

statement ok
ATTACH 'ducklake:{DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION}' AS ducklake (DATA_PATH '{DATA_PATH}/repro_partition_retry/', METADATA_CATALOG 'metadata', DATA_INLINING_ROW_LIMIT 0);

statement ok
USE ducklake;

statement ok
SET immediate_transaction_mode=true

statement ok
COPY (
    SELECT 1 AS id, 'google_ads_data_hub' AS source, 10 AS value
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 2 AS id, 'google_ads_data_hub' AS source, 20 AS value
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 3 AS id, 'bing' AS source, 30 AS value
) TO '{DATA_PATH}/repro_slice.parquet' (FORMAT parquet);

statement ok con1
USE ducklake;

statement ok con2
USE ducklake;

statement ok con1
BEGIN;

statement ok con1
CREATE TABLE first_write AS SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{DATA_PATH}/repro_slice.parquet') LIMIT 0;

statement ok con1
ALTER TABLE first_write SET PARTITIONED BY (source);

query I con1
DELETE FROM first_write WHERE source IN ('google_ads_data_hub');
----
0

statement ok con1
INSERT INTO first_write BY NAME SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{DATA_PATH}/repro_slice.parquet');

# concurrent unrelated commit forces con1's first commit attempt to fail retryably
statement ok con2
CREATE TABLE unrelated_table(i INTEGER);

statement ok con1
COMMIT;

query I con1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM first_write;
----
3

query I
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM metadata.ducklake_data_file
WHERE table_id >= 9223372036854775808 OR partition_id >= 9223372036854775808;
----
0

# every committed data file must reference a partition id that exists
# (materialize the partition ids first - scanner-backed metadata catalogs do not
# support multiple streaming scans in one query)
statement ok
SET VARIABLE known_partition_ids = (
    SELECT LIST(partition_id)
    FROM metadata.ducklake_partition_info
);

query I
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM metadata.ducklake_data_file
WHERE partition_id IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT list_contains(getvariable('known_partition_ids'), partition_id);
----
0

# same scenario on a pre-existing table: re-partition + insert with a concurrent snapshot mid-transaction
statement ok con1
BEGIN;

statement ok con1
ALTER TABLE first_write SET PARTITIONED BY (id);

statement ok con1
INSERT INTO first_write BY NAME SELECT * FROM read_parquet('{DATA_PATH}/repro_slice.parquet');

statement ok con2
INSERT INTO unrelated_table VALUES (1);

statement ok con1
COMMIT;

query I con1
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM first_write;
----
6

query I
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM metadata.ducklake_data_file
WHERE table_id >= 9223372036854775808 OR partition_id >= 9223372036854775808;
----
0

statement ok
SET VARIABLE known_partition_ids = (
    SELECT LIST(partition_id)
    FROM metadata.ducklake_partition_info
);

query I
SELECT COUNT(*)
FROM metadata.ducklake_data_file
WHERE partition_id IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT list_contains(getvariable('known_partition_ids'), partition_id);
----
0

name: Config Tests
on:
  push:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  repository_dispatch:
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.head_ref || '' }}-${{ github.base_ref || '' }}-${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  ducklake-config-tests:
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.draft == false
    name: DuckDB Tests with DuckLake + DuckDB Back-End
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        arch: ['linux_amd64']
        vcpkg_version: [ '2023.04.15' ]
        include:
          - arch: 'linux_amd64'
            vcpkg_triplet: 'x64-linux'

    env:
      VCPKG_TARGET_TRIPLET: ${{ matrix.vcpkg_triplet }}
      GEN: Ninja
      VCPKG_TOOLCHAIN_PATH: ${{ github.workspace }}/vcpkg/scripts/buildsystems/vcpkg.cmake
      DUCKLAKE_CI: 1

    steps:
    - name: Install required ubuntu packages
      run: |
        sudo apt-get update -y -qq
        sudo apt-get install -y -qq build-essential cmake ninja-build ccache python3 mold

    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
        submodules: 'true'

    - name: Checkout DuckDB to version
      run: |
        cd duckdb
        git checkout $(cat ../.github/duckdb-version)

    - name: Setup Ccache
      uses: hendrikmuhs/ccache-action@main
      with:
        key: ${{ github.job }}
        save: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' || github.repository != 'duckdb/ducklake' }}

    - name: Setup vcpkg
      uses: lukka/run-vcpkg@v11.1
      with:
        vcpkgGitCommitId: a42af01b72c28a8e1d7b48107b33e4f286a55ef6

    - name: Build extension
      env:
        GEN: ninja
      run: |
        make release

    - name: Test extension
      env:
        DUCKDB_TPCH_ANSWERS_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/duckdb/extension/tpch/dbgen/answers
      run: |
        build/release/test/unittest --test-config test/configs/attach_ducklake.json --test-dir duckdb

# name: test/sql/retry/postgres_localized_conflict_retry.test
# description: a primary key conflict on Postgres is retried when the server reports errors in another language
# group: [retry]

require ducklake

require parquet

require postgres_scanner

require-env DUCKLAKE_CI

require-env DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION

test-env DATA_PATH {TEST_DIR}

statement ok
ATTACH '{DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION}' AS pg

statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS localized_retry CASCADE')

statement ok
ATTACH 'ducklake:{DUCKLAKE_CONNECTION}' AS dl
(DATA_PATH '{DATA_PATH}/localized_retry', METADATA_SCHEMA 'localized_retry')

statement ok
SET ducklake_retry_wait_ms = 1

statement ok
CREATE TABLE dl.t (i INT)

# the next snapshot insert fails once with the Polish message for a duplicate key
statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'CREATE SEQUENCE localized_retry.attempts;
CREATE FUNCTION localized_retry.fail_once() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
	IF nextval(''localized_retry.attempts'') = 1 THEN
		RAISE unique_violation USING MESSAGE =
			''podwójna wartość klucza narusza ograniczenie unikalności "ducklake_snapshot_pkey"'';
	END IF;
	RETURN NEW;
END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
CREATE TRIGGER fail_once BEFORE INSERT ON localized_retry.ducklake_snapshot
FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION localized_retry.fail_once()', prepare = false)

statement ok
INSERT INTO dl.t VALUES (1)

query I
SELECT * FROM dl.t
----
1

# an error that names no DuckLake primary key is still not retried
statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION localized_retry.fail_once() RETURNS trigger AS $$
BEGIN
	PERFORM nextval(''localized_retry.attempts'');
	RAISE unique_violation USING MESSAGE =
		''podwójna wartość klucza narusza ograniczenie unikalności "inny_klucz"'';
END $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql')

statement error
INSERT INTO dl.t VALUES (2)
----
inny_klucz

# nor when the failed query mentions one
statement ok
BEGIN

statement ok
CALL dl.set_commit_message('author', 'ducklake_snapshot_pkey')

statement ok
INSERT INTO dl.t VALUES (2)

statement error
COMMIT
----
inny_klucz

# one attempt for each of these inserts after two for the first one
query I
SELECT last_value FROM postgres_query('pg', 'SELECT last_value FROM localized_retry.attempts')
----
4

statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'DROP TRIGGER fail_once ON localized_retry.ducklake_snapshot')

statement ok
INSERT INTO dl.t VALUES (3)

query I
SELECT * FROM dl.t ORDER BY ALL
----
1
3

statement ok
DETACH dl

statement ok
CALL postgres_execute('pg', 'DROP SCHEMA localized_retry CASCADE')

# DuckDB DuckLake Extension DuckLake is an open Lakehouse format that is built on SQL and Parquet. DuckLake stores metadata in a [catalog database](https://ducklake.select/docs/stable/duckdb/usage/choosing_a_catalog_database), and stores data in Parquet files. The DuckLake extension allows DuckDB to directly read and write data from DuckLake. See the [DuckLake website](https://ducklake.select) for more information. ## Installation DuckLake can be installed using the `INSTALL` command: ```sql INSTALL ducklake; ``` The latest development version can be installed from `core_nightly`: ```sql FORCE INSTALL ducklake FROM core_nightly; ``` ## Usage DuckLake databases can be attached using the [`ATTACH`](https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/statements/attach.html) syntax, after which tables can be created, modified and queried using standard SQL. Below is a short usage example that stores the metadata in a DuckDB database file called `metadata.ducklake`, and the data in Parquet files in the `file_path` directory: ```sql ATTACH 'ducklake:metadata.ducklake' AS my_ducklake (DATA_PATH 'file_path/'); USE my_ducklake; CREATE TABLE my_ducklake.my_table(id INTEGER, val VARCHAR); INSERT INTO my_ducklake.my_table VALUES (1, 'Hello'), (2, 'World'); FROM my_ducklake.my_table; ┌───────┬─────────┐ │ id │ val │ │ int32 │ varchar │ ├───────┼─────────┤ │ 1 │ Hello │ │ 2 │ World │ └───────┴─────────┘ ``` ##### Updates ```sql UPDATE my_ducklake.my_table SET val='DuckLake' WHERE id=2; FROM my_ducklake.my_table; ┌───────┬──────────┐ │ id │ val │ │ int32 │ varchar │ ├───────┼──────────┤ │ 1 │ Hello │ │ 2 │ DuckLake │ └───────┴──────────┘ ``` ##### Time Travel ```sql FROM my_ducklake.my_table AT (VERSION => 2); ┌───────┬─────────┐ │ id │ val │ │ int32 │ varchar │ ├───────┼─────────┤ │ 1 │ Hello │ │ 2 │ World │ └───────┴─────────┘ ``` ##### Schema Evolution ```sql ALTER TABLE my_ducklake.my_table ADD COLUMN new_column VARCHAR; FROM my_ducklake.my_table; ┌───────┬──────────┬────────────┐ │ id │ val │ new_column │ │ int32 │ varchar │ varchar │ ├───────┼──────────┼────────────┤ │ 1 │ Hello │ NULL │ │ 2 │ DuckLake │ NULL │ └───────┴──────────┴────────────┘ ``` ##### Change Data Feed ```sql FROM my_ducklake.table_changes('my_table', 2, 2); ┌─────────────┬───────┬─────────────┬───────┬─────────┐ │ snapshot_id │ rowid │ change_type │ id │ val │ │ int64 │ int64 │ varchar │ int32 │ varchar │ ├─────────────┼───────┼─────────────┼───────┼─────────┤ │ 2 │ 0 │ insert │ 1 │ Hello │ │ 2 │ 1 │ insert │ 2 │ World │ └─────────────┴───────┴─────────────┴───────┴─────────┘ ``` See the [Usage](https://ducklake.select/docs/stable/duckdb/introduction) guide for more information. ## Building & Loading the Extension To build, type ``` git submodule init git submodule update --recursive # to build with multiple cores, use `make GEN=ninja release` make ``` The submodules are pinned to the DuckDB version in `.github/duckdb-version`, which is what CI builds against. `make pull` moves them to the tip of their branch instead, where the build can fail. To run, run the bundled `duckdb` shell: ``` ./build/release/duckdb ``` ## Contributing We are happy to welcome external contributions to our DuckLake extension. Our active development branch is currently `main`, and all contributions should target that branch. ## Testing ```bash # run all DuckLake extension tests ./build/release/test/unittest # run a single test file ./build/release/test/unittest test/sql/transaction/create_conflict.test # run tests matching a pattern ./build/release/test/unittest "test/sql/partitioning/*" # run DuckDB core tests using DuckLake as storage backend ./build/release/test/unittest --test-config test/configs/attach_ducklake.json --test-dir duckdb # run DuckLake tests using PostgreSQL as catalog database (requires running PostgreSQL) ./build/release/test/unittest --test-config test/configs/postgres.json # run DuckLake tests using SQLite as catalog database ./build/release/test/unittest --test-config test/configs/sqlite.json # run tests with deletion vectors enabled ./build/release/test/unittest --test-config test/configs/deletion_vectors.json ``` ### Code Coverage `make codecov` builds `build/codecov`, a release build in which only the DuckLake sources are instrumented for clang's source-based code coverage, like `make codecov` in DuckDB. DuckDB's test runner then writes the coverage report of the tests it runs, by default the fast ones. It needs `llvm-profdata`, `llvm-cov` and `genhtml` from lcov 2.0 to 2.5 (2.2 and 2.6 fail on its options). Run it from the repository root, so the report only shows `src`: ```bash python3 duckdb/scripts/ci/run_tests.py build/codecov/test/unittest --coverage-report build/codecov/coverage/fast # any test runner argument works, e.g. the tests with SQLite as catalog database python3 duckdb/scripts/ci/run_tests.py build/codecov/test/unittest --coverage-report build/codecov/coverage/sqlite \ --test-config test/configs/sqlite.json "test/sql/*" ``` CI merges the coverage of the tests of every metadata catalog (DuckDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite and Quack) into the `coverage-ducklake` artifact, and fails a pull request that lowers the line coverage of the latest report of `main`.
